_comment: AOS Sprint 6 — the five deterministic demand-signal categories. 'keywords' are matched case-insensitively, whole-phrase, against an article's title+summary (same convention as opportunity-relevance-engine.md and market-intelligence-classification-model.md's six checks) to decide which categories a signal belongs to — pure text matching, no model call. 'baseScore' feeds demand_engine.py's weighted Overall Demand Score aggregation. Edit this file to retune categories/keywords/scores — no code change needed.

aggregationWeights._note: Overall Demand Score = min(100, weighted sum). Each matched category contributes its baseScore times this weight; multiple matched categories aggregate (a company matching more categories scores higher, but with diminishing per-category weight so no single very-high-scoring category alone can't exceed 100, and stacking several confirms rather than just repeats one signal).

buyingReadinessBands._note: 0-100 score bucketed into the four bands Part 4 requires.

buyingReadinessWeights._note: Deterministic weighted formula, each component 0-10, weights sum to 1.0. See demand_engine.py's compute_buying_readiness_score().

nextActionByBand._note: Deterministic first pass; demand_engine.py's recommend_next_action() overrides this for failure/regulatory triggers regardless of band, since those warrant faster action than a generic band mapping would suggest.

categoryToServices._note: Deterministic ranked service prediction per category, in priority order. Names are Service Mapping Engine's own canonical primaryServices (service-mapping/runtime/config/service-catalogue.json) — reused, not a second taxonomy invented for Demand Intelligence. Where the founder's brief used a near-synonym (e.g. 'ADGL Readiness Assessment', 'AI Compliance Assessment'), the closest canonical entry is used instead so every part of AOS names services the same way.

governanceNeedByCategory._note: The 'organisations at this stage typically require...' clause in the templated Opportunity Narrative (demand_engine.py's build_opportunity_narrative()) — factual, not marketing copy.
governanceNeedByCategory.ai_adoption: governance around deployment assurance, human oversight, operational controls, privacy, monitoring and AI risk management
governanceNeedByCategory.governance_trigger: structured governance operating models, policy frameworks and independent assurance that the new function or programme is complete and defensible
governanceNeedByCategory.funding_trigger: an AI governance operating model and readiness assessment established before the newly-funded AI expansion scales beyond what informal oversight can manage
governanceNeedByCategory.regulatory_trigger: a compliance assessment and control framework mapped directly to the named regulatory obligation, plus independent third-party risk review where vendors are involved
governanceNeedByCategory.failure_trigger: an independent risk assessment, root-cause review and control-framework remediation to prevent recurrence and demonstrate the issue has been addressed
